title: Sowing basil microgreens
subtitle: How to sow a basil microgreen tray — including the no-soak, no-surface-water rule
excerpt: Basil seed must be sown dry, not pre-soaked. When wet, basil seeds form a gel coating that makes them impossible to distribute evenly. Sow basil seed dry onto a pre-dampened medium and do not water from above.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Penn State Extension indoor herb growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: The gel layer that forms around basil seeds when they are exposed to water. Basil seeds are mucilaginous: when wet, each seed quickly develops a transparent gelatinous coating. This is a normal property of the seed and aids germination, but causes problems in microgreen growing if seeds are pre-soaked or surface-watered, as the seeds stick together in an unmovable mass.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. For basil, use only a light cover — not a heavy weight — as the fine seedlings are easily damaged.

content.text: Basil microgreens are sown differently from most other microgreen crops. The seed must go into the tray dry, not pre-soaked, and must not be watered from above at any point during the growing cycle. The reason is a gel coating that forms around each seed when it contacts water.

: when basil seed contacts water, each seed rapidly develops a transparent gel coating. Dry basil seed is small and scatters easily. Wet basil seed turns into a sticky clump that cannot be distributed evenly. Pre-soaking basil seed before sowing makes it impossible to sow in a consistent layer.

One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray. A second tray for the blackout cover (no weight, unlike most crops). Seed compost, pre-dampened. Basil seed: 10 to 15 g per tray (less than most microgreen crops, as basil seed expands in moisture).

Step 1: pre-dampen the seed compost. Mix water into the compost until it holds together when squeezed but does not drip. This pre-dampening is essential: basil seed must not be surface-watered after sowing.
Step 2: fill the tray with pre-dampened compost to within 1 cm of the rim. Level the surface.

Step 3: scatter dry basil seed at 10 to 15 g per tray. Basil seed is tiny; use a pinch-and-scatter motion from 20 cm above the tray to get even distribution. The seeds will absorb moisture from the medium and begin to swell within 20 to 30 minutes of sowing.
Step 4: do not press. Unlike most microgreen seeds, basil seeds do not benefit from pressing; the fine seeds sit on or just at the surface and pressing risks burying them too deep.

: rest a second tray lightly on top. Do not add weight; basil seedlings are very fine and a heavy cover can damage the emerging shoots. Place in a warm location (above 20°C if possible). Leave for two to three days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with basil microgreens.

items.symptom: Seeds clumped together in a gel mass when sowing
items.cause: Seeds touched water before being scattered, or the medium surface was wet when sowing.
items.fix: Always sow basil seed dry. If the seeds have already gelled, they cannot be separated without damage. Start with a fresh tray and dry seed.

items.cause: Uneven distribution of the fine seed, or room too cold.
items.fix: Scatter from higher above the tray (25 cm) on the next attempt for better distribution. Confirm the room temperature is above 18°C; basil seed germinates very slowly in a cool room.

items.symptom: Seedlings collapsed at the base within the first two days of blackout
items.cause: Damping off triggered by surface moisture or poor airflow around the tray.
items.fix: Ensure the medium was pre-dampened but not waterlogged. Do not cover the tray with a tight plastic cover that traps moisture; a second tray with ventilation gaps is better. Ensure some airflow when the tray is removed to light.
